p: Nebo stoopeth: These were the chief idols of Babylon.
beasts: Because they were of gold and silver, the Medes and Persians carried them away.
They stoop: The beasts that carried the idols fell down under their burden.
themselves have gone into captivity: He derides the idols, who had neither soul nor sense.
borne by me from the birth: He shows the difference between the idols and the true God; for they must be carried by others, but God himself carries his, as in De 32:11.
have made: Seeing I have begotten you, I will nourish and preserve you forever.

compare me: The people of God setting their own calamity, and the flourishing estate of the Babylonians, would be tempted to think that their God was not so mighty as the idols of their enemies: therefore he describes the original of all the idols to make them to be abhorred by all men: showing that the most that can be spoken in their commendation, is but to prove them vile.
mind: Become wise, meaning, that all idolaters are without wit or sense, like mad men.
bird from the east: That is, Cyrus, who will come as swift as a bird and fight against Babylon.
counsel from a far country: Him by whom I have appointed to execute that which I have determined.
righteousness: Who by your incredulity would prevent the performance of my promise.
near my righteousness: He shows that man's incredulity cannot abolish the promise of God, Ro 3:3.
